page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled directly with the instance, consisting of a 1920 GB local NVMe SSD. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a strong single-core compute profile, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier. Multi-core performance, however, aligns with the average tier, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth remains consistently in the average range, reaching 117.28 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 69.27 GB/sec for large block write operations. In database and application-level tests, the server maintains average performance, executing 15.09 million Redis SET operations per second and achieving a static web serving throughput of 8.4 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop to the bottom 25% for 7B model prompt processing.

The server offers a balanced qualitative cost-efficiency profile for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources with a generous 1920 GB NVMe SSD. The primary tradeoff lies in its moderate multi-core scaling and average memory bandwidth, which may limit its effectiveness for highly parallelized high-performance computing or large-scale AI model inference. This hardware configuration is well-suited for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring dedicated CPU resources and substantial local NVMe storage.
